facts.text: The Ashland Historical Association preserves the town’s landmarks and runs a library and research center where visitors can view historic documents.
The town’s website offers a treasure trove of old photos and information that chronicles Ashland’s rich history.
As a non‑profit, the Ashland Historical Association is dedicated to preserving and promoting the town’s history through programs and publications.
Community volunteers on the Association’s board acquire and manage artifacts, ensuring they remain accessible for research and education.
Ashland sits in Chemung County, New York, and is one of several towns sharing the name across the United States.
The town’s official website notes a state‑wide burn ban that is in effect through May 14, 2026, for all residents.
